svg.title: CCOF DR: original Azure icons and private network boundaries
svg.desc: Proposed two-region Standard v2 gateways behind Front Door Premium; Cosmos and Log Analytics are outside customer VNets, with private endpoint connections.

text.tspan: CCOF | Active/passive DR with private Standard v2 gateways and multiple Foundry backends
PROPOSED DESIGN - not deployed or failover-qualified. Original Microsoft Azure service icons; no customer-specific addresses.
VNet links, hub peering and DNS forwarding
DNS links alone do not provide connectivity
Front Door is the public edge.
they are not NICs in the customer VNet.
Serving; services sit outside the VNet.
Timers ON; one active writer set; Cosmos leases
Graph group reads; budgetState writes; authoritative ledger queries
Only delegated integration subnets and private endpoint NICs are inside.
Undelegated; endpoint NICs only, not service instances.
+ Function sites and per-app blob private endpoints
Warm standby; services sit outside the VNet.
Timers OFF until fenced promotion + ledger continuity gate
Graph group reads; budgetState writes; authoritative ledger queries
Only delegated integration subnets and private endpoint NICs are inside.
Undelegated; endpoint NICs only, not service instances.
+ Function sites and per-app blob private endpoints
Private endpoints F-A; local priority 1 in pool A
Private endpoints F-B; local priority 1 in pool B
Each pool: member breaker opens -> skip; cooldown -> permit again.
One workspace ID; not inside a customer VNet.
Scope for both regional Monitor PEs; private log queries
Azure-managed replication; typically ~2 minutes, not guaranteed
Both APIMs: diagnostic ingestion uses a managed Microsoft channel (not the Monitor PE)
KQL queries need the AMPLS-connected corporate/VDI path
COSMOS DB - ONE ACCOUNT / TWO REGIONS
Managed data-plane boundary, not a customer VNet.
Replica promoted on configured service-managed failover
Standby writers remain fenced until promotion
Dashed blue: customer VNet / subnet. Solid service boxes: PaaS outside VNet. Only PE NICs sit inside PE subnets. Azure replication is not VNet peering.
